overview: Angola's women's health innovation is driven mainly by government, UN agencies and donors rather than a dense startup market, with progress against high maternal mortality as the central theme. Digital tools such as the SMS-based Monami pregnancy programme and the Safe Delivery App are being layered onto public maternity services, while 2025 brought Angola's first national HPV vaccination campaign and continued menstrual health pilots. A young startup ecosystem, newly supported by a Startup Law and incubation programmes, includes the health-access platform Appy Saude, though dedicated femtech and gender-lens capital remains thin.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent milestones center on cervical cancer prevention, postpartum haemorrhage care and falling maternal mortality.

items.text: Angola launched its first national cervical cancer (HPV) vaccination campaign, aiming to protect more than two million girls aged 9-12, with a school and health-centre phase from 27 October to 7 November 2025.
Thirty-four health professionals completed a Training of Trainers on postpartum haemorrhage; Angola became the first country to implement WHO's new PPH guideline, with UNFPA and Norway support.
Angola reported a decline in maternal and child mortality, with the maternal mortality ratio falling from 239 to around 160-170 per 100,000 live births per INE survey and WHO 2025 data.
CNN profiled Appy Saude, Angola's largest online pharmacy network, reporting roughly 95% year-on-year growth and expansion beyond Angola.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: National strategies and UN country programmes frame the maternal, reproductive and startup agenda.

items.text: Angola's National Maternal and Neonatal Health Strategy 2023-2027 aims to expand quality obstetric care and strengthen antenatal and postpartum services.
UNFPA is implementing its 9th Country Programme (2024-2028) in Angola, targeting zero preventable maternal deaths, zero gender-based violence and zero unmet need for family planning.
Angola aligned its cervical cancer effort with WHO's global elimination strategy targets (90% of girls vaccinated, 70% screened, 90% treated by 2030).
Angola's National Assembly unanimously approved a Startup Law creating a legal framework, a startup seal, pre-seed/seed/Series A incentives and a National Startup Council.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Most women's-health innovation is delivered through donor-backed digital tools and incubation programmes.

items.text: The Monami programme (Lucrecia Paim and Manuel Pedro Azancot de Menezes maternity hospitals) sends weekly pregnancy SMS; about 30,000 pregnant women registered in its first year, with 95%+ reporting they learned something new.
UNFPA and MINSA rolled out the Safe Delivery App, training 240 health workers across drought-hit Huila, Cunene, Namibe and Cuando Cubango; it is expected to support tens of thousands of births.
Government, UNFPA and BeGirl Inc. ran a Menstrual Health Management pilot, equipping 1,000 girls aged 10-16 with menstrual panties and giving tracking tools to 1,000 girls and 1,000 boys.
INAPEM and INFOSI signed an MoU (March 2025) to run the DIGITAL.AO incubation programme, offering startups incubation space, training, mentorship and investor access.
Appy Saude expanded internationally, launching operations in Rwanda with Kenya targeted, exporting its health-information and online pharmacy model.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The landscape mixes public maternity institutions, UN agencies, a leading health-tech startup and startup-support bodies.

items.name: Appy People
items.note: Tech firm that built the Monami maternal-health SMS programme

items.name: Maternidade Lucrecia Paim
items.note: Luanda maternity hospital co-leading the Monami pregnancy programme

items.name: Ministry of Health (MINSA)
items.note: Runs national maternal/neonatal strategy, HPV campaign and Safe Delivery App rollout

items.name: UNFPA Angola
items.note: Lead UN partner on maternal health, family planning, PPH and menstrual health programmes

items.name: UNICEF Angola
items.note: Supports maternal and child health and menstrual dignity initiatives for adolescent girls

items.name: BeGirl Inc.
items.note: Partner on Angola's menstrual health management pilot providing menstrual products and tracking tools

items.name: INAPEM
items.note: SME agency co-running the DIGITAL.AO incubation programme for startups
